transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the 08:00 change-control huddle. As you know, Welding Cell 5 is running on a controller firmware version that hits end of vendor support this month, and we have a tentative firmware retrofit scheduled for Friday before the cell's next production run. Before I authorize the work, I need to hear from controls engineering, production planning, and quality on any relevant requirements or concerns. Let's start with controls engineering — what do we need to know about the firmware retrofit?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety requirement. I confirmed with the controller vendor yesterday that a safety bulletin identifies an interlock race condition in the current firmware. This means the retrofit must be completed before Welding Cell 5's next production run — it's not just a support lifecycle issue, it's a safety issue. The work requires exactly 6 hours of energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation. I also want to note that the vendor bulletin has not yet been attached to the work order, so we need to get that documented before proceeding.

transcript.text: I need to share my production-capacity check results. Alternate Welding Cell 4 can produce exactly 160 of the 240 assemblies needed for the Friday customer order by Friday 16:00, but the remaining 80 assemblies must be produced on Cell 5 after the retrofit. There's a critical timing constraint: the Cell 4 reservation expires Thursday at noon, and I have not yet entered the temporary reservation in the production system. So we need to lock in that Cell 4 reservation today, and the Cell 5 retrofit needs to be completed in time for those remaining 80 assemblies to be produced before the Friday deadline.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical customer quality requirement. I verified in the customer's quality portal that exactly the first 20 assemblies produced after a controller change must be held for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release. This requirement has not yet been copied into our local inspection plan, so it's not reflected in any of our current procedures. This means after the Cell 5 firmware retrofit, the first 20 assemblies off the line cannot be released to the customer until they pass that validation. Given Marta's plan for 80 assemblies on Cell 5 post-retrofit, we need to account for this hold in our production and delivery timing.

commitments.detail: Attach the vendor safety bulletin to the work order before proceeding with the retrofit.
Enter the temporary Cell 4 reservation in the production system today, before the Thursday noon expiration, to secure capacity for 160 assemblies.
Complete the 6-hour energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation on Cell 5 in time for the remaining 80 assemblies to be produced before the Friday deadline.
Copy the customer's post-controller-change validation requirement (first 20 assemblies held for weld-macro and dimensional validation) into the local inspection plan.
Plan for the first 20 assemblies produced on Cell 5 post-retrofit to be held for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release to the customer.
Record the authorization decision and assign all follow-up actions for scheduling, execution, and documentation.
